publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: I am deeply sensible of the honour you have conferred on me by electing me President of the Institute, and I realise fully that the confidence thereby expressed imposes responsibilities. I earnestly trust that during my term of office the high traditions of the Institute, so worthily upheld by past Presidents, will lose nothing in influence or dignity. It would hardly be human not to be deeply moved and not to feel pride and pleasure in the high position which this Institute now holds, representing, as it does, all phases of electrical interests in South Africa. This is a fine achievement, which, with the help of the Council, it will be my endeavour to maintain and advance constantly. I gladly accept your confidence and the responsibilities imposed.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In contributing to this discussion, in the first place, .I think .Mr. Monk might make it quite clear in his reply that he only intended to touch upon one or two aspects of the somewhat complex problem of automatic protection. Quite obviously he designed his paper to be mildly provocative; I think he set out to draw opinions and arguments from the mining side of power supply on these fields. He has not been very successful up to date, because the discussion on his paper can only be described as scanty, and I wonder if I might be permitted to assist him in his attempts at provocation. I would first like to suggest that in any future papers he writes on the subject, in which he is virtually a specialist, he might be better advised to follow Mr. Heydorn's example and write a paper on a single aspect of the protection question. For instance, a review of modern methods and developments in the automatic protection of a single interconnected distribution network would, to my mind, be of great value and afford this Institute much useful information which to-day is probably on record in a number of papers read before various Institutes, but the information is difficult of access, and could with advantage be collected into a single paper, if only for record purposes.

articleTitle: The ammonia, nitric acid and sulphuric acid concentration plants of messrs. African explosives amp; industries, limited, at modderfontein, transvaal
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, this is a somewhat unusual paper to read before an Institute of Electrical Engineers, but it was felt, in view of the forthcoming visit of the Institute to the Dynamite Factory, that that visit would be made more interesting if some brief outline were given of the processes to be seen. For those who think-that nothing but electrical matters should be read or discussed at a meeting of this kind, I will ask you to look on this plant as a consuming device, and, in support of that, I would say that the consumption of energy will be over 10 million units during the first year, and the load factor about 85 per cent. The plant is of very considerable importance to this country, in that the institution of it has reduced the importation of certain raw materials and substituted locally produced material for those imports. For instance, coke now takes the place of nitrate of soda; in addition, the plant provides employment for something like 71 whites and 61 natives on the operating staff alone, quite independently of those who are engaged on the services, and it also forms a basis for expansion, inasmuch as the plants can be utilised to provide nitrogenous fertilisers and make use of carbon dioxide, which is one of the by-products.

articleTitle: A graphical, representation of the operation of a tandem generator
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper discusses the operation in parallel of two alternators driven in tandem. The set is installed in the Brak-pan station of The Victoria Falls amp; Transvaal Power Company, Limited, where one single cylinder type turbine, capable of developing a continuous maximum output of 20,000 kw. and a most economical output of 16,000 kw. when running at a normal speed of 3,000 r.p.m. is directly coupled to a 20,000 kVA generator known as the “A” unit, and coupled to the latter is another 20,000 kVA generator designated the “B” unit. Beyond the “B” unit and driven on the same shaft are two compound wound exciters, one for the “B,” the other for the “A” unit. The total overall length of the set from the extreme end of the turbine to the sole-plate at the exciter end is 63 feet 8 12 inches, and the average width across the sole-plate of a generator is approximately 12 feet. The first two photographs show views of the set in the engine room at the Brakpan Power Station.
